summary.summary: This is the REVISED, pre-approval version of Appendix A to North Northamptonshire's 2025/26 Annual Governance Statement (AGS), going to the Audit and Governance Committee. The Council judges its governance arrangements generally effective, providing a moderate level of assurance, with 71% of 13 tracked 2024/25 governance actions implemented during the year (page 21); the rest — timely closure of internal-audit actions, social-care/DSG financial sustainability, consistent safeguarding controls, and assurance over shared services/partnerships — carry forward as live risks for 2026/27. It notes an overall revenue overspend against the 2025/26 budget in demand-led adults' and children's social care, partially offset by earmarked reserves, though no monetary figures are given in this narrative document (page 9). Against the Draft appendix (queue E06000061-7f338f1e), this REVISED copy adds one short paragraph on the Corporate Scrutiny Committee's review of performance/budget-monitoring reports (page 9) but is otherwise near-identical in substance.

compliance.notes: Scored from the complete Executive pack of 10 February 2026 (TMSS cover report plus Appendices A-E) together with the General Fund Final Budget/MTFP/Capital Programme report and its Budget Book, which carries the Capital Investment Strategy at pp.111-131. The Council HAS a Housing Revenue Account — Appendix B para 5.18 describes HRA self-financing for the legacy Kettering and Corby stock with loans assigned to one fund or the other and an Item 8 charge between the General Fund and the HRA; Appendix C charges no MRP on HRA assets and budgets £1.000m of HRA loan repayment; para 6.1 budgets £3.3m of HRA debt interest; and the capital programme includes £61.665m of HRA capital expenditure. HRA-conditional requirements were therefore scored as applicable, and the Council is marked down on two of them (no separate HRA liability benchmark, LB-04; and a General-Fund-only financing-costs ratio with no HRA equivalent, PI-07). Strongest areas by some distance: the liability benchmark (Table 2 plus an Arlingclose chart to 2075 with all four balances), the treasury investment strategy and counterparty framework, and governance/practices — Appendix E is a full 62-page TMP1-TMP12 document with schedules, a role-by-role dealing authorisation matrix and named external providers, which most authorities never publish. Weakest area: the non-treasury/commercial family in the 5-page Appendix D, where proportionality is recited but never demonstrated, no ratio of commercial income to net revenue stream is produced, no monetary limit caps commercial property investment, and the specified/non-specified analysis is inconsistent with the long-dated instruments the TMSS approves. The separate HRA Budget 2026-27 report was not in the pack but suppresses nothing scored here.

gaps.evidence: Appendix B p.11 para 5.11 table and Budget Book p.131 Table 11: financing costs £10.4m/£10.1m/£10.1m/£10.0m/£9.9m; proportion of net revenue stream 2.96% / 2.33% / 2.18% / 2.05% / 1.89% (2025/26 forecast to 2029/30)

Appendix E TMP6 p.39 lists 'Net income from commercial and service investments to net revenue stream' among the prudential indicators the Council will cover in its annual strategy documents; Appendix D p.5 Table 5 gives rates of return (commercial property 4.69%) but not as a ratio to the net revenue stream

Appendix E TMP3 p.25 and Appendix B para 3.14 restate the substance of Prudential Code paras 51–53 (no borrowing to invest primarily for financial return; PWLB certification), but no document contains a compliance statement citing paragraphs 51 to 53

Cover report para 4.6 and Appendix E TMP3 p.24 recite the principle that 'the risks of the Council's commercial investments should be proportionate to the Council's overall capacity — ie that plausible losses could be absorbed in budgets or reserves without unmanageable detriment to local services'; Appendix D para 3.2 sets service-loan limits 'to ensure that total exposure to service loans remains proportionate to the size of the Council'; Appendix D p.5 Table 4 gives total investment exposure of £157.896m (31.3.25) falling to £34.691m (31.3.27)

Appendix D p.2 Table 1 approved limits on service loans — subsidiaries £2.000m, local businesses £1.000m, local charities £0.500m, employees £0.500m, other £0.500m; p.3 Table 2 approved limit on shares in subsidiaries £2.000m

news_drafts.headline: North Northamptonshire forecasts a £22.988m General Fund overspend for 2026/27 at quarter 2
news_drafts.lead:
North Northamptonshire Council is forecasting an overspend of £22.988m on its General Fund for 2026/27, according to the quarter 2 finance and performance report for its Executive meeting on 10 November. The General Fund is the main account, paid for by council tax and business rates, covering services other than council housing and schools.

The report sets out the order in which the council will respond. Officers will first seek in-year efficiencies to reduce the overspend. The contingency budget and reserves are available to call on afterwards.

The paper names demand-led social care and travel to school transport as the main risks.

findings.headline: Strategic risk TPMO 2 on delivering transformation programmes within timescales and benefits has a residual score of 5 (Amber), and its action to establish the Transformation Board in September 2026 is still listed as a gap in the November 2026 register.
findings.detail: Inherent scoring was Very High impact, Possible likelihood, 15 (Amber). Residual scoring is Very High impact, Very rare likelihood, 5 (Amber). The register says a PMO project framework has been introduced and that the Transformation Board launches in September. The listed action to establish the board in September 2026 remains under gaps in this November 2026 version.
findings.matters: It shows a dated governance action and a large reduction in scored risk, and a finance director would want to see whether the board was in place by the date set.
findings.figures: Inherent: Very High impact, Possible, 15 (Amber). Residual: Very High impact, Very rare, 5 (Amber).
findings.quote: Establish the Transformation Board in September 2026 to govern the project framework

findings.headline: Strategic risk LEIS 10 on bringing leisure in-house records that 'All potential costs not yet known' and that timeframes are tight, with residual score 12 (Amber).
findings.detail: The Executive decided on 11 Aug 26 to bring all NNC leisure facilities in house under NNC Leisure service management during 27-28, then transform them into a single service. The risk is that the programme is not delivered within existing contract end dates or the existing budget envelope. The gaps column also says detailed action plans for each working group are required.
findings.matters: A service moving in-house with costs not yet known is a budget exposure a finance officer elsewhere would want to track.
findings.figures: Inherent: High impact, Likely, 16 (Red). Residual: High impact, Possible, 12 (Amber).
findings.quote: All potential costs not yet known.

findings.headline: Strategic risk FINA 20 records a diagnostic review carried out with NCT, NNC and WNC on emerging pressures in children's social care, with the risk scored 20 (Red) residual.
findings.detail: The risk concerns financial pressure and performance issues at the North Northamptonshire Children's Trust creating additional exposure and budget pressure for the council. The register records that a diagnostic review was carried out in partnership with NCT, NNC and WNC, and lists monitoring of placement market trends as an ongoing action.
findings.matters: Children's social care pressure through a trust arrangement is a common source of unplanned council cost, and this shows one council's partnership response to it.
findings.figures: Inherent: Very High impact, Very Likely, 25 (Red). Residual: High impact, Very Likely, 20 (Red).
findings.quote: Diagnostic review has been carried out in partnership with NCT/NNC/WNC around emerging pressures in children’s social care

findings.headline: Strategic risk FINA 12 names budget overspends and depletion of reserves as its risk, scored 20 (Red) residual with a gap to review reserves adequacy annually.
findings.detail: The risk covers demand-led service pressures, inflation, contractual commitments and emerging financial pressures. Controls include monthly budget monitoring, a Budget Recovery Framework, directorate challenge sessions and the Reserve Strategy. The listed action to develop mitigations via diagnostic reviews for emerging pressures is still a gap.
findings.matters: It shows the council's own assessment that overspends could deplete reserves, and the controls it relies on to prevent that.
findings.figures: Inherent: Very High impact, Very Likely, 25 (Red). Residual: High impact, Very Likely, 20 (Red). Reserves adequacy reviewed annually.
findings.quote: Failure to effectively manage demand-led service pressures, inflation, contractual commitments and emerging financial pressures results in budget overspends and depletion of reserves.

findings.headline: Strategic risk FINA 13 on medium-term financial sustainability is scored 20 (Red) after controls, with residual likelihood Very Likely, down from 25 (Red) inherent.
findings.detail: The register states the risk as future resources being insufficient for service demand, statutory obligations and corporate priorities. Controls listed include the Medium Term Financial Strategy, the Transformation Programme, the savings programme and the Reserve Strategy. Gaps listed include refreshing the MTFS regularly and strengthening savings delivery governance.
findings.matters: A finance director at this or another council can compare how the register scores the medium-term position and which savings and reserve controls it relies on.
findings.figures: Inherent: Very High impact, Very Likely, 25 (Red). Residual: High impact, Very Likely, 20 (Red).
findings.quote: Future resources are insufficient to meet service demand, statutory obligations and corporate priorities, resulting in an unsustainable financial position over the medium term.
